item.content:encoded:
The Tampa Bay Rays, the New York Yankees, and the Boston Red Sox have all punched their ticket to the postseason. With the final week of the 2026 MLB regular season already upon us, several other American League squads are playing for a place in October, too.
Even the Rays and Yankees technically have to decide who wins the AL East, with the former enjoying a hefty advantage heading into the final week, needing just one win over the Bombers to secure it. After that, there are two wide-open divisions and an exciting competition for the last Wild Card spot.
Here’s where every team stands in the race:
Tampa Bay Rays
Remaining games: 4 @ Yankees, 3 @ Phillies
Current record: 95-60
Current position in division/Wild Card race: 1st in AL East (6 games ahead of NYY)
Final week outlook: The Rays have been, far and away, the top team in the American League by win-loss record, and unless something really crazy happens, they will enter the postseason with a first-round bye and wait for the winner of the battle between the top two Wild Cards—the Yankees and Red Sox—in the Division Series. They’ll still try to play competitive games after clinching, as they certainly wouldn’t say no to having home-field advantage over NL teams in a potential World Series matchup* as they seek their first championship in franchise history, but the pressure this week is much lighter.
*We’re keeping the focus on the AL in this post, but for those curious, Tampa Bay’s 95-60 record currently trails the Dodgers’ 96-60 and the Brewers’ 98-58. Atlanta trails at 92-64. The Dodgers have the Padres and Giants to end 2026 while the Brewers have the Phillies and Cardinals, and the Braves have the Reds and Marlins.
New York Yankees
Remaining games: 4 vs. Rays, 3 vs. Orioles
Current record: 89-66
Current position in division/Wild Card race: 2nd in AL East (6 games behind TB); 1st in Wild Card race (5.5 games ahead of 2nd Wild Card spot, held by BOS)
Final week outlook: Unless they sweep the Rays and Orioles, the Yankees virtually have no chance of winning the AL East crown. Instead, they will likely enter the postseason as the top Wild Card team, as they have a healthy cushion over the Red Sox, their likely foe in the Wild Card round. The odds of that series being at Fenway rather than Yankee Stadium are extremely low, especially since New York has the tiebreaker over Boston.
Boston Red Sox
Remaining games: 3 vs. Guardians, 3 vs. Cubs
Current record: 84-72
Current position in division/Wild Card race: 3rd in AL East, 2nd in Wild Card race (5.5 games behind NYY for top WC spot, 4 games ahead of CHW, owners of the 3rd WC spot)
Final week outlook: The Red Sox are highly unlikely to move from the second AL Wild Card spot, since they have a four-game cushion over the White Sox, owners of the third slot, and are 5.5 games behind the Yanks for the top one. They’ve been all but locked into this spot for awhile now and just clinched their playoff berth yesterday with Houston’s loss to Atlanta.
Cleveland Guardians
Remaining games: 3 @ Red Sox, 3 @ Royals
Current record: 81-75
Current position in division/Wild Card race: 1st in AL Central (1 game ahead of CHW)
Final week outlook: Eyeing their third consecutive division title and seventh since 2016, the Guardians are currently one game up in the race for the AL Central, but need to avoid a tie with the White Sox at the top because Chicago owns the tiebreaker. Cleveland is peaking at the right time, though, and José Ramírez is finally starting to show some signs of a breakthrough at the plate. If that’s the case, they will be dangerous with a strong young core and two aces at the top: AL strikeout leader Gavin Williams and Rookie of the Year contender Parker Messick. Second baseman Travis Bazzana isn’t too shabby of a rookie, either.
Chicago White Sox
Remaining games: 3 @ Royals, 3 vs. Rockies
Current record: 80-76
Current position in division/Wild Card race: 2nd in AL Central (1 game behind CLE), 3rd in Wild Card race (3 games ahead of HOU and TOR, 5 ahead of BAL)
Final week outlook: Chicago’s lack of quality starting pitching seems to have caught up to them in September, but they are still a dangerous team that is trending towards its first postseason appearance since 2021. They have a chance to win the AL Central: all they need to do is finish in at least a tie with the Guardians, and though both the Pale Hose and Guards will face the Royals this week, the Southsiders have an easier other foe in the Rockies. Remember, winning the division would likely even give Chicago the second seed in the AL and a first-round bye to face the victor of the AL West/last Wild Card matchup.
It’s already been an improbably great season for the White Sox, as merely getting a winning season would’ve been a huge success for a team that lost a modern record 121 games in 2024 and 102 last year. But missing out at this point would still be quite the disappointment.
Texas Rangers
Remaining games: 3 vs. Mets, 3 @ Twins
Current record: 78-78
Current position in division/Wild Card race: 1st in AL West (1 game ahead of HOU)
Final week outlook: If the Rangers finish with more wins than the Astros, they will capture the AL West despite their thoroughly mediocre record (the Mariners’ deeply disappointing 2026 really made the division a mess). It’s a key week in Texas, as the range of outcomes is wide: they could win the division and finish as high as the second seed if they can best the AL Central champ’s line; they could be the final Wild Card squad, or they could miss the playoffs entirely for the third year in a row since winning it all in 2023 behind two-time World Series MVP Corey Seager.
It’s important to note that the Rangers need to beat the Astros by at least one game to take the AL West crown because Houston owns the tiebreaker. The Rangers own tiebreakers against the Orioles, Guardians, and Blue Jays, and lost against the White Sox and, as explained, the Astros. The AL West winner is a near-lock to face the worst Wild Card team in the first round, though they will host the best-of-three.
Toronto Blue Jays
Remaining games: 3 @ Orioles, 3 vs. Reds
Current record: 77-79
Current position in division/Wild Card race: tied with HOU for 4th in Wild Card standings, 3 games behind the 3rd spot (CHW)
Final week outlook: Last year’s AL champs can’t win their division: their only path to the playoffs is the third and final Wild Card spot. With that in mind, however, they would need to finish ahead of both the White Sox and the Rangers because both of them own the tiebreaker against Toronto. It sure doesn’t help that ace Dylan Cease was scratched from his next start and is undergoing an MRI.
The Jays tied the season series against Houston, which, in the event of a tie at the third WC spot between them, would take us to intra-divisional record to decide. There, Toronto is 25-24 against AL East opponents, and the Astros are 22-24 vs. AL West foes, presently giving the Jays the edge, though that could change this week since they both face intra-divisional rivals.
For what it’s worth, Toronto won the tiebreakers against the Guardians and the Orioles.
Houston Astros
Remaining games: 2 @ Mariners, 4 @ A’s
Current record: 77-79
Current position in division/Wild Card race: tied with TOR for 4th in Wild Card standings, 3 games behind the 3rd spot (CHW)
Final week outlook: Much like the White Sox in the AL Central, the Astros are one game behind in their division and own the tiebreaker against the Rangers, so all they need to do is catch them by the end of the week. They have lost three straight, though, with a -59 run differential, so despite the best efforts of MVP frontrunner Yordan Alvarez, they aren’t particularly good. We have seen plenty of mediocre squads make it in the past, so they definitely have a chance — especially since they get to play the mostly-hapless M’s and A’s this week.
Houston can still qualify via the last Wild Card, but the division presents a smoother path. Since we’re running through them, they own tiebreakers vs. the White Sox, Guardians, and Rangers, losing vs. the Orioles and tying vs. Toronto.
Baltimore Orioles
Remaining games: 3 vs. Blue Jays, 3 @ Yankees
Current record: 75-81
Current position in division/Wild Card race: 6th in Wild Card standings, 5 games behind the 3rd spot (CHW)
Final week outlook: At this point, the Orioles need a miracle to get in. They needed to sweep the Brewers this past weekend to put themselves in a position to compete. Instead, they got swept themselves. Baltimore won tiebreakers against the White Sox and the Astros, and lost against the Rangers, Guardians, and Blue Jays. But again, they have essentially no shot whatsoever. That final weekend series in the Bronx could’ve been interesting; alas.

item.title: [fansided.com] MLB Power Rankings: Playoff stakes rise as October contenders make their move
item.dc:creator: Chris Landers; Mark Powell
item.description: The playoffs technically don't start for another week or so, but good luck telling that to teams for which every game already feels like October. With the standings in both the NL and AL as jumbled as they've been in recent memory, the stakes are already as high as can be — and whoever gets hot now could well ride that wave all the way to a World Series. "Hot" could definitely describe both the San Diego Padres and Cleveland Guardians of late. The former has decided to just never lose again, not
item.content:encoded:
The playoffs technically don't start for another week or so, but good luck telling that to teams for which every game already feels like October. With the standings in both the NL and AL as jumbled as they've been in recent memory, the stakes are already as high as can be — and whoever gets hot now could well ride that wave all the way to a World Series.
"Hot" could definitely describe both the San Diego Padres and Cleveland Guardians of late. The former has decided to just never lose again, not only grabbing hold of a Wild Card spot but now pushing for home-field in the first round if things break right. The latter, meanwhile, has once again snatched the AL Central while no one was looking. And they're not the only ones making serious moves in our latest MLB power rankings.
But who are we buying as serious title contenders, and who still has work to do? Read on to find out.
30. Colorado Rockies
The Rockies have admittedly let go of the rope of late, well on their way to yet another 100-loss season. There are at least some promising young hitters in this organization, which represents something to build upon moving forward. Of course, the pitching staff remains a mess, and no one's been able to crack that nut yet in Colorado.
–Chris Landers, FanSided.com editor
29. Los Angeles Angels
In Reid Detmers, Walbert Urena and Ryan Johnson, the Angels have at least some sort of foundation upon which to build for the future. Well, OK, maybe not Detmers, who will almost certainly be dealt this offseason. But still, L.A.’s pitching staff has been a real bright spot of late. The offense … well, that’s another question. Things are going to get worse before they get better under John Mozeliak. At least Arte Moreno is no longer around to meddle in it.
–CL
28. Athletics
The A’s are playing out the string of a lost season, although the contributions they’ve gotten from young bats like Henry Bolte, Max Muncy (not that one), Lawrence Butler and Zack Gelof down the stretch have been notable. None of that will matter, though, until the team fixes its pitching staff. We know we sound like a broken record, but it really is that simple, and no potential answers have emerged in the second half.
–CL
27. San Francisco Giants
Rafael Devers' injury, which figures to cost him at least some of next season as well as the end of this one, is a fitting if unfortunate end to what's been a miserable season by the Bay. Devers had been one of the few bright spots on this Giants team down the stretch alongside Bryce Eldridge; now, it's unclear how San Francisco will rebuilt its offense for 2027 in addition to finding reinforcements for a pitching staff that simply hasn't been good enough.
–CL
26. Kansas City Royals
The Kansas City Royals have been eliminated for quite some time now. If there is one clear goal for Kansas City this winter, it's to build a roster around Bobby Witt Jr. that is capable of making a postseason run. That is every team's goal, but the Royals are so far away from contention despite featuring such a prolific player, Witt Jr.'s career is closer to becoming Mike Trout's than Derek Jeter's.
-Mark Powell, FanSided.com MLB director
25. Minnesota Twins
At one point not all that long ago, the Twins had a realistic chance to make the playoffs as the third AL Wild Card spot. Then, the bottom fell out. Byron Buxton underwent successful hip surgery just last week that will keep him out until spring training, whenever that may be. The Twins once again experienced the roster flaw of building around an injured star.
-MP
24. New York Mets
This week couldn’t have been more awkward for the New York Mets when Pete Alonso hit his 300th home run in his return to Citi Field, much to the delight of many Mets fans in attendance, but once Alonso left town, the Mets began to play better, winning two games in a row against the Phillies. Those wins, headlined by more quality play from youngsters like Carson Benge, Zac Thornton and Christian Scott, show why Mets fans should be somewhat enthusiastic for what’s to come.
–Zach Rotman, FanSided.com staff writer
23. Cincinnati Reds
In the American League, the Reds likely wouldn't be the worst team in their division. But the NL Central has been a gauntlet all year long, and the Reds couldn't keep up. Despite breakthrough seasons from Elly De La Cruz and Sal Stewart, Cincinnati still has a long way to go on the starting pitching front. Can they rely on Hunter Greene and Chase Burns moving forward?
-MP
22. Seattle Mariners
Going 3-3 against the Angels and Rockies this week just about sums up this season in Seattle. The good news is that youngsters like Michael Arroyo and Lazaro Montes have helped to key an offensive turnaround. The bad news is that the starting rotation hasn’t held up its end of the bargain of late, and there are still tons of long-term questions about this lineup — especially with Randy Arozarena set to hit free agency. Jerry DiPoto will need to find some answers this offseason after a year in which just about everything went wrong.
–CL
21. Washington Nationals
The Washington Nationals deserved a better fate in 2026. Even with their offense falling off a bit of late, they’re still third in the majors in runs scored. The dynamic duo of CJ Abrams and James Wood is as good as any in the National League. Recently extended Cade Cavalli is a budding ace. Andrew Alvarez has thrown the ball incredibly well and looks like a future rotation stalwart. If it weren’t for a historically bad bullpen, we’d be talking about this team in Wild Card contention.
–ZR
20. Detroit Tigers
The Tigers have the best run differential in the AL Central and a pythagorean record of an AL playoff team. None of it matters. Scott Harris and the Tigers front office gave up on their team's postseason hopes at the trade deadline. Then, they proceeded to get fans' hopes up with a late August run, only to play like the team Harris assumed they'd become when it mattered most. The Tigers have some work to do, though the emergence of young stars in the lineup like Hao-Yu Lee and Kevin McGonigle, paired with Riley Greene's consistent play, give them some building blocks.
-MP
19. St. Louis Cardinals
The Cardinals are ahead of schedule, but not a postseason team. Make no mistake about it, St. Louis came crashing back down to earth in September, and has been eliminated from playoff contention. There are questions about the long-term future of Masyn Winn, especially with JJ Wetherholt as the de-facto shortstop of the future. But these are all good problems to have. Now, if only Bloom could find an ace burried in that farm system of his.
-MP
18. Baltimore Orioles
A series against league-best Milwaukee came at the worst possible time for the O’s, which now find themselves needing to hit an inside straight to snatch the final Wild Card spot. Pete Alonso’s heroics at Citi Field aside, Baltimore’s bats simply have not been good enough. Heck, no part of this team has; they’re hovering around .500 for a reason, after all, and there’s no reason to think they have the consistency required to get hot over the final week and overtake the White Sox, Blue Jays and Astros.
–CL
17. Miami Marlins
The Miami Marlins tried to do what they could to stick around in the NL postseason hunt, even using Sandy Alcantara on one day of rest in a save opportunity, but they were eliminated following Friday’s loss in San Diego. As disappointing as that is, the Marlins could finish above .500 for just the third time since 2009. That’s a sign that things are heading in the right direction for Miami.
–ZR
16. Toronto Blue Jays
The Jays have lost three of four series now, and news that Dylan Cease will have his next start bumped due to shoulder fatigue makes it even less likely that Toronto can sneak its way into the playoffs. With Trey Yesavage and Shane Bieber already on the IL, the rotation has begun leaking oil, and that’s not something this power-starved lineup is equipped to handle. The Jays still have a path to the final Wild Card spot, but it’s becoming an increasingly tenuous one, and it’s hard to see them making much noise even if they did get in.
–CL
15. Houston Astros
Getting swept at home by the Braves this weekend might well wind up costing the Astros a playoff spot. The closing schedule isn’t too tough, with trips to Seattle and Sacramento on tap. Still, if Houston doesn’t figure out where its high-powered offense went before it’s too late — and if Joe Espada can’t stop his bullpen from blowing late leads — Yordan Alvarez’s MVP season may well be for nought. As it stands, this looks like a team with fatal flaws that will spoil what could have been a deep run in a wide-open AL.
–CL
14. Chicago White Sox
Reality hit the White Sox real quick. Chicago has lingered around .500 for longer than they'd care to admit, and it was only a matter of time before the rest of the Central caught up to them. Munetaka Murakami has been dreadful since the trade deadline, and thus any contract extension talks have been put on hold. If the White Sox can hold on to a playoff spot, they'll be one of the best stories in October. If not, this season could all be for naught.
-MP
13. Texas Rangers
All of a sudden, the Rangers find themselves back in control of the AL West and home-field advantage in the first round of the playoffs. Of course, that says more about the West than it does about Texas; this is still a .500 team, one without a ton of depth on either side of the ball. The interesting thing, though, is that this lineup has finally started to show signs of life of late. Take care of business against the Twins and Mets this week, and no one’s going to want to face a team with Jacob deGrom and Nathan Eovaldi in the rotation plus an offense featuring Corey Seager, Wyatt Langford and Josh Jung.
-CL
12. Pittsburgh Pirates
The narrative Pirates fans are spinning these days is the same web every National League non-playoff team will get caught in this week; if only we played in the American League! Yes, the disparity between leagues is easy to blame for the Pirates shortcomings, but the front office also fell short in acquiring bullpen arms last winter, which could've kept Pittsburgh from blowing an extraordinary number of leads in the season's first half. That'll haunt these Pirates forever.
-MP
11. Arizona Diamondbacks
It's not Arizona's fault that their primary competition for a Wild Card spot, San Diego, has become one of the hottest teams in baseball over the last few weeks. Either way, though, Arizona has simply run out of bullets, especially in a rotation that hasn't gotten the boost from Corbin Burnes' return that they were hoping for. Eduardo Rodriguez has turned back into a pumpkin, and there's just not enough depth to keep pace with what's become a beast of an NL playoff chase.
–CL
10. Cleveland Guardians
Here we go again with the Guardians. Cleveland is a legitimate threat in a weak American League. Much like last season, the Guards are taking advantage of a fellow contender floundering down the stretch. This is when Cleveland plays its best baseball, so it should be no surprise they've won five straight games heading into Monday's potential postseason preview against the Red Sox.
-MP
9. Boston Red Sox
Dropping consecutive series to the Rangers and Rays won’t do much to Boston’s postseason outlook — they’ve been more or less locked into a Wild Card series in the Bronx for a while now — but it still doesn’t inspire confidence in this team’s ability to make a run come October. This offense is once again mired in a power outage, and while getting Willson Contreras and others back from the IL figures to help, who knows when that might actually be. And there’s still just a real dearth of power here that even this pitching staff might not be able to make up for.
–CL
8. Philadelphia Phillies
I don’t know what to think of the Philadelphia Phillies. On one hand, a rotation led by Zack Wheeler, Cristopher Sanchez, a healthy Jesus Luzardo, a rejuvenated Aaron Nola and a much-improved Andrew Painter should will them to wins. On the other hand, Luzardo is not healthy, the lineup is top-heavy and the bullpen, outside of Jhoan Duran, is an utter disaster. The Phillies are almost certainly going to make the playoffs, but their losses in New York this week ruined any last hope they had at a division title. And with how they’re playing right now, I don’t know if I’d pick them to get beyond the Wild Card Round.
–ZR
7. Chicago Cubs
The Cubs playoff parade was put on hold Sunday as Alex Bregman was struck in the face by a foul ball. Bregman was taken to the local hospital, and it's unclear how much time he will miss as of this writing. Chicago's postseason hopes may hang in the balance, as their one clear advantage over every other NL team is their lineup. The Cubs have scored the most runs in baseball this year.
-MP
6. San Diego Padres
Yes, the schedule has helped, particularly series against Miami, Colorado, Washington, San Francisco and Cincinnati. But no matter who they've played, the Padres look like a different team from the one we saw for much of the year, with their big bats finally mashing and their rotation coming into focus with Nick Pivetta now back in the fold. San Diego is now dead even with Chicago and Philly in the Wild Card race, and no one will want to face this lineup and this bullpen in a short series.
–CL
5. New York Yankees
Just when it seemed like New York was getting ready to make a move, with Aaron Judge finally back in the lineup after months on the shelf, the reigning AL MVP landed right back on the IL — this time with a calf strain that could well jeopardize his entire postseason. It’s been that sort of year for the Yankees, which have the pitching to keep believing in them as contenders but just haven’t been able to put it all together enough to take command of their own playoff destiny. And with a Judge-less offense and a penchant for mistake-filled baseball, winning three series in a row feels like a tough ask even in this AL.
–CL
4. Atlanta Braves
The Atlanta Braves punched their ticket to the playoffs this week, and thanks to the Phillies’ struggles, they’re on the cusp of winning the NL East — ensuring a top-three seed in the National League. Tyler Mahle pitched another gem, and Ronald Acuña Jr. is hitting his stride at the perfect time. There’re still some concerns with the team, like the No. 3 spot in their rotation and struggling stars like Austin Riley and Ozzie Albies, but getting to the playoffs is a big deal, and the Braves can take pride in checking that box.
–ZR
3. Tampa Bay Rays
The Rays may well have sewn up the AL East this week, taking two of three from the Red Sox over the weekend to stretch their lead over the Yankees ahead of an all-important four-game set in the Bronx beginning on Tuesday. Even if New York were to sweep all four, though, Tampa would still have the inside track to the division and the No. 1 overall seed. This pitching staff continues to thrive beyond all expectation even with some recent injuries, and the hitting has done just enough. Whether that recipe will withstand the postseason is the only question now.
–CL
2. Los Angeles Dodgers
Don't look now, but L.A.'s lineup has begun to stir, with Kyle Tucker looking like the player the Dodgers thought they were paying for this offseason. They also got Edwin Diaz back this week, and he's suddenly looking like the star closer of old — potentially answering this team's biggest question entering October. We know the rotation will be there; if they have Tucker at the height of his powers and a one-two punch in Diaz and Tanner Scott at the end of games, the three-peat march might be back on.
–CL
1. Milwaukee Brewers
The Brewers set a franchise record with 98 wins on Sunday. They still have a full week to go to add to that mark, and appear likely to reach the 100-win plateau. That's a great accomplishment, but it won't mean squat if Milwaukee falls to the Los Angeles Dodgers — or any other NL team for that matter — on their way to that elusive NL pennant. The Brewers are the favorites, but the Dodgers are lingering right behind them.
-MP

item.title: [FanGraphs] Bobby Witt Jr. and the Off-Peak MVP Season
item.dc:creator: Davy Andrews
item.description: Bobby Witt Jr. is having a down year. He’s running his worst batting line in three seasons. He’s in danger of missing the 20-homer threshold for the first time in his career. A lower back injury in July will also limit him to a career low in games played. Put it together, and Witt is on pace to put up his the lowest WAR total since his 5.9-win 2023 campaign. Oh, and he also grabbed hold of the American League lead in WAR back in July and still hasn’t relinquished it. A down year by Bobby Witt Jr
item.content:encoded:
Bobby Witt Jr. is having a down year. He’s running his worst batting line in three seasons. He’s in danger of missing the 20-homer threshold for the first time in his career. A lower back injury in July will also limit him to a career low in games played. Put it together, and Witt is on pace to put up his the lowest WAR total since his 5.9-win 2023 campaign. Oh, and he also grabbed hold of the American League lead in WAR back in July and still hasn’t relinquished it. A down year by Bobby Witt Jr.’s standards is still good enough to make him a deserving MVP.
I don’t know if Witt is going to win his first MVP this year. Ours is the only flavor of WAR in which he leads the AL, and he leads by just a quarter of a win. He ranks third by Baseball Reference’s rWAR and is eighth by Baseball Prospectus’ WARP. Yordan Alvarez leads all of baseball in WARP because he’s hitting like, well, Yordan Alvarez and staying healthy like, well, someone other than Yordan Alvarez. Cam Schlittler leads the AL in Baseball Reference WAR, and he’s been so dominant that he deserves consideration for the Cy Young-MVP combo — if only he’d pitched just 23 fewer innings last year, he could’ve gone for the trifecta with Rookie of the Year. Kevin McGonigle has played like an MVP from the moment he arrived in Detroit, and Junior Caminero has surpassed 40 home runs for the second season in a row as a 23-year-old. All of these guys have a case, and they aren’t the only ones who merit inclusion in the discussion:
| Name | fWAR Rk | fWAR | rWAR Rk | rWAR | WARP Rk | WARP | Avg Rk | Avg WAR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bobby Witt Jr. | 1 | 6.6 | 3 | 6.5 | 8 | 5 | 4 | 6.0 |
| Yordan Alvarez | 2 | 6.4 | 4 | 6.4 | 1 | 7.3 | 2 | 6.7 |
| Cam Schlittler | 3 | 6.1 | 1 | 7 | 3 | 5.8 | 2 | 6.3 |
| Dylan Cease | 4 | 5.5 | 8 | 5.7 | 12 | 4.6 | 8 | 5.3 |
| Miguel Vargas | 5 | 5.2 | 10 | 5.3 | 2 | 5.9 | 6 | 5.5 |
| Junior Caminero | 6 | 5.2 | 7 | 5.7 | 5 | 5.3 | 6 | 5.4 |
| Kevin McGonigle | 7 | 5.1 | 2 | 6.7 | 4 | 5.3 | 4 | 5.7 |
| Randy Arozarena | 8 | 5.1 | 11 | 5.3 | 16 | 4 | 12 | 4.8 |
| Dillon Dingler | 9 | 4.6 | 25 | 4 | 23 | 3.3 | 19 | 4.0 |
| Drew Rasmussen | 10 | 4.6 | 21 | 4.2 | 13 | 4.4 | 15 | 4.4 |
| Reid Detmers | 11 | 4.6 | 35 | 3.7 | 11 | 4.7 | 19 | 4.3 |
| Parker Messick | 13 | 4.6 | 6 | 5.8 | 9 | 4.8 | 9 | 5.1 |
| Pete Alonso | 14 | 4.2 | 18 | 4.3 | 6 | 5.3 | 13 | 4.6 |
| Ceddanne Rafaela | 21 | 3.9 | 9 | 5.4 | 94 | 1.7 | 41 | 3.7 |
| Gavin Williams | 27 | 3.7 | 46 | 3.1 | 7 | 5.2 | 27 | 4.0 |
| Wilyer Abreu | 32 | 3.4 | 5 | 5.8 | 20 | 3.6 | 19 | 4.3 |
| Mike Trout | 40 | 3.2 | 28 | 3.9 | 10 | 4.8 | 26 | 4.0 |
Pete Crow-Armstrong, Jacob Misiorowski, Schlittler, McGonigle and JJ Wetherholt have made the AL MVP the only major award that’s really in question). If you want to read a particularly good example, you should check out the one Mario Delgado Genzor wrote for Baseball Prospectus on Friday. I want to focus on something slightly different — namely, how good Witt has already been in years when he missed out on an MVP and how unusual it would be for him to win it this year.
(A quick note before we get into it: We’re about to spend a lot of time talking about WAR. I know I mentioned rWAR and WARP earlier. They’re an important piece of the puzzle, especially due to the outsized effect rWAR in particular has on the MVP conversation, but from here on out, we’re sticking with good old FanGraphs WAR.)
This is Witt’s fifth major league season, and you could argue that it’s his fourth consecutive MVP-caliber campaign. Mind you, that argument would focus only on 2022, in which he put up 5.9 WAR, good for 10th in the majors. There’s no argument to be had about the 2024 and 2025 seasons. That said, along with Shohei Ohtani’s combined 9.2-WAR 2022 sesaon, they are the two most valuable seasons this decade for which a position player did not win an MVP. In 2024, Witt ran a 169 wRC+, stole 31 bases, and put up a Fielding Run Value of 11, fourth among all shortstops. That was good for 10.5 WAR, and it took the best season of Aaron Judge’s career – 58 home runs, a 19% walk rate, and a .322 batting average – to beat him. In 2025, Witt put up 8.0 WAR with a 130 wRC+, 38 steals, and 20 FRV, the best mark among all shortstops. Again, he was bested by a 10-win season from Judge and Cal Raleigh’s 60-homer campaign. Witt has never received a first place MVP vote.
Crow-Armstrong, who has the National League MVP all but locked down, gives us a great example of what it normally takes to win an MVP award. He may even finish with 10.5 WAR through his excellence in all three phases of the game, just like Witt did in 2024. Players like Judge, Ohtani, and Mike Trout, whose base level of talent is so high that a healthy campaign is almost sure to keep them a step above the rest of the league, don’t come around all that often. Even when they do come around, they still need to be playing at something close to their peak, and peaks don’t last that long. Until Ohtani, the only player to win more than three MVPs was Barry Bonds, whose regimen for raising and widening his peak has been well documented. Sometimes that’s because of voter fatigue, but often it’s because somebody else popped up with an amazing, undeniable season like PCA’s. Most of the time, the MVP is an already great player for whom everything goes perfectly. They stay healthy and they play not just their best, but over their heads. Think of Ronald Acuña Jr. winning the NL MVP in 2023 with 9.1 WAR, 4.1 more than his next-best total, or Mookie Betts winning the AL MVP in 2018 with 10.2 WAR, 2.8 more than his next-best total.
Generally speaking, since the voting started getting more rigorous in the last couple decades, those are the two categories of players who win MVPs. We see all-time greats who perform like only they are capable of performing, and we see excellent players who put it all together in a blaze of glory. Witt’s 2024 season probably falls into that second category. He wasn’t quite at his defensive or baserunning peak, but he put up his best season at the plate by nearly 40 points of wRC+ and DRC+, and he ended up with an all-timer of a season. His 10.5 WAR tied for the 36th-best position player campaign of all time. His company? Willie Mays and Babe Ruth twice apiece, Barry Bonds, and Rogers Hornsby. Unfortunately, he ran into one of those special players from the first category, in the form of Judge. If Witt had put up those 2024 numbers this year, he’d be en route to a unanimous MVP just like PCA.
But I said “in theory” earlier, and I said it because Witt isn’t done yet. He’s still just 26, and if not for those weeks he missed with back tightness, or a wOBA that’s more than 30 points below his xwOBA, he’d now be wrapping up his third straight seven-plus-win season. He’s elite in every facet of the game and he doesn’t look like he’s in danger of slowing down any time soon. It wouldn’t be much of a shock to see him rediscover his nine- or 10-win form. In other words, there’s at least a chance Witt belongs to that first category of player and not the second.
Earlier I mentioned Acuña and Betts claiming MVPs by putting up the best years of their careers by a long shot. That’s pretty standard. Especially in recent years, it’s awfully rare for a player to take home an MVP award in something other than the best season of their career, unless they also won the MVP in the best year of their career. Leaving those multi-time MVPs out (and excluding 2020 for obvious reasons), here’s the whole list of players who won an MVP in a year that wasn’t their best by fWAR since 2011: Giancarlo Stanton and Paul Goldschmidt.
Goldschmidt put up 6.8 WAR in his 2022 NL MVP season and 7.2 in 2015. In that sense, Goldschmidt fit a third archetype: the established star who doesn’t put up their biggest WAR total, and instead wins MVP as something of a career achievement award. Stanton put up 6.5 WAR in 2017, not quite the 6.8-win campaign he put up in 2014, but he was facing a weaker field, he was more established as a star, and he had the cachet of a 59-homer season. We’re talking about gaps of less than half a win. We had some multi-time winners, but Acuña, Betts, Cody Bellinger, Christian Yelich, Jose Altuve, Kris Bryant, Josh Donaldson, Andrew McCutchen, and Buster Posey all won MVP in the best seasons of their career by fWAR.
Let’s say that Witt does win the MVP this year. For the sake of round numbers, let’s say he closes strong and finishes with 7.0 WAR. That would be just the third-best season of his career, and a full 3.5 WAR below his career-high. Baseball Reference lists MVP winners going back to 1911, and in that time, Witt would become just the ninth position player to win MVP in a season that trailed their best year by such a wide margin. The list of players to do it before him is full of three-time MVPs like Joe DiMaggio, Mickey Mantle, and Mike Schmidt. Not only that, but you’ll note that if Witt does make this list, the only higher number in either column will belong to Mantle:
| Player | MVP Year | MVP WAR | Best Year | Best WAR | Difference |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frankie Frisch | 1931 | 4.1 | 1927 | 9.7 | 5.6 |
| Mickey Mantle | 1962 | 6.0 | 1956 | 11.5 | 5.5 |
| Willie Stargell | 1979 | 2.7 | 1971 | 8.2 | 5.4 |
| Joe DiMaggio | 1947 | 4.8 | 1941 | 9.7 | 4.9 |
| Freddie Freeman | 2020* | 3.0 | 2023 | 7.7 | 4.7 |
| Robin Yount | 1989 | 5.3 | 1982 | 9.8 | 4.5 |
| Andre Dawson | 1987 | 3.5 | 1982 | 7.3 | 3.8 |
| Mike Schmidt | 1986 | 5.8 | 1974 | 9.4 | 3.6 |
| Roger Peckinpaugh | 1925 | 2.4 | 1919 | 5.9 | 3.5 |
The last person to do so was Robin Yount, who won the AL MVP with 9.8 WAR in 1982, and then again with 5.3 WAR in 1989, long before anybody knew that Total Zone considered him the 11th-worst defender in the majors. This hasn’t happened in nearly 30 years, and Witt is in a very different boat here. He’s not one of the two MVP favorites because his season looks great to the eye but doesn’t fool the advanced metrics. He’s not an aging star who can count on some lifetime-achievement votes. He’s a young gun who’s leading his league in WAR because he excels in every facet of the game.
I realize that this is far from the most meticulous analysis I’ve ever conducted, and that MVP voting is and should be about more than WAR. Still, I hope I’ve put this season in the context it deserves. By our measuring stick, Witt has been the best player in the American League this season. He’s done so despite missing time due to injury. He’s done so despite some bad batted ball luck. And he’s done so despite not even coming close to the highest gear we know he’s got available to him, because that gear is so high that it’s normally reserved for inner-circle Hall of Famers. However the voting goes, Witt’s been in MVP form for three or four years now.
Davy Andrews is a Brooklyn-based musician and a writer at FanGraphs. He can be found on Bluesky @davyandrewsdavy.bsky.social.

item.content:encoded:
CLEVELAND -- - Gavin Williams threw seven shutout innings, Jo Adell had an RBI infield single and the Cleveland Guardians beat the Athletics 1-0 Sunday to remain atop the AL Central.
Steven Kwan added three hits for Cleveland, which posted its seventh series sweep of the season and third at home.
The Guardians (81-75) are one game in front of the Chicago White Sox, who defeated Detroit 8-1. They finish the season on the road with series against Boston and Kansas City.
Williams (14-8) gave up three hits and struck out nine to move into the American League lead with 244 strikeouts. Toronto's Dylan Cease is in second with 239. It is the 13th time in 31 starts this season that the right-hander has had at least nine strikeouts.
Cade Smith worked 1 1/3 innings for his 39th save in 44 opportunities.
The Athletics were swept for the second straight series and lost all six games on their road trip.
José Ramírez led off the fourth with a double down the right-field line, advanced to third on Chase DeLauter's fly out to left and scored on Jo Adell's infield single. Pitcher Jack Perkins (3-12) fielded the soft grounder on the grass in front of the mound, but his throw hit Adell in the back as he was in the basepath.
Athletics manager Mark Kotsay was ejected for the third time this season for agruing the call.
Perkins went six innings and allowed one run on four hits.
The Athletics' best chance came in the eighth inning when they had runners on second and third with one out. Hunter Gaddis struck out pinch-hitter Carlos Cortes and Smith whiffed Henry Bolte.
Up next
Athletics: Return home to face the Los Angeles Angels on Tuesday. LHP Brady Brasso (1-3, 4.50 ERA) will take the mound.
Guardians: LHP Parker Messic (12-9, 2.57 ERA) goes on Tuesday to start a three-game series at Boston.
------

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dylan Cease undergoes MRI on right shoulder, may not start again this season as Blue Jays fight for wild-card playoff spot
item.dc:creator: Ian Casselberry
item.description: The Toronto Blue Jays may be without their ace starting pitcher as they pursue a playoff berth during the final week of the 2026 MLB regular season. Dylan Cease underwent an MRI exam on his right shoulder Saturday night and has been scratched from his start scheduled for Wednesday against the Baltimore Orioles. Blue Jays manager John Schneider told reporters Sunday that Cease could be shut down for the remainder of the season. Going into Sunday's play, Toronto (76-79) was three games behind the
item.content:encoded:
The Toronto Blue Jays may be without their ace starting pitcher as they pursue a playoff berth during the final week of the 2026 MLB regular season.
Dylan Cease underwent an MRI exam on his right shoulder Saturday night and has been scratched from his start scheduled for Wednesday against the Baltimore Orioles. Blue Jays manager John Schneider told reporters Sunday that Cease could be shut down for the remainder of the season.
Going into Sunday's play, Toronto (76-79) was three games behind the Chicago White Sox (79-76) for the American League's third and final wild-card playoff spot. The Houston Astros are one game ahead of the Blue Jays in the standings at 77-78. Toronto has a 4.2% chance of making the postseason, according to FanGraphs.
.@thehazelmae and @ArdenZwelling provide the latest on Dylan Cease and the Blue Jays' pitching plan as they try to stay alive in the AL Wild Card race. pic.twitter.com/hhaPPLdHea
— Sportsnet (@Sportsnet) September 20, 2026
If Cease's MRI shows no serious concerns, it's possible that he could make one more start during the regular season's final three-game series with the Cincinnati Reds. But if the Blue Jays are too far back in the playoff race by then, it's unlikely Cease would pitch again.
Schneider explained that Cease has been dealing with an issue in his shoulder for several weeks and has been throwing with less velocity. The eight-year veteran described the problem as shoulder fatigue, according to Schneider.
In his start Friday versus the Texas Rangers, Cease's fastball was clocked as low as 90 mph and he pitched only 2 2/3 innings in a 7-1 loss. He finished with 6 walks and 3 strikeouts, allowing 1 earned run and 6 hits.
"It wasn't alarming enough to say, 'Hey, I can't pitch,' and was hoping to kind of come out of it," Schneider said, via The Athletic, "But just really hasn't bounced back. So I think [we] just said, 'All right, let's take a look at it.'"
Cease, 30, is in the first year of a seven-year, $210 million contract he signed with the Blue Jays in November.
He is second in the AL with a 2.40 ERA and trails only Milwaukee's Jacob Misiorowski among MLB pitchers with 239 strikeouts. Overall, he has an 11-6 record in 29 starts, pitching 169 innings.

item.content:encoded:
The Toronto Blue Jays are looking to avoid being swept by the Texas Rangers on Sunday and have made some changes to their lineup.
Toronto is coming off a 6-2 loss on Saturday after losing 7-1 on Friday. The two losses seemingly ended the Blue Jays' playoff hopes.
The Blue Jays are now 76-79.
Toronto Blue Jays Announce Brandon Valenzuela News
Toronto is looking to avoid the series sweep and has made some major changes to its lineup.
The Blue Jays are resting some regular players, as starting catcher Alejandro Kirk is getting the day off, with Brandon Valenzuela getting the start. He will also be hitting eighth.
Toronto's lineup on Sunday is as follows:
- B. Bateman CF
- V. Guerrero Jr. 1B
- N. Lukes RF
- K. Okamoto 3B
- S. Keys DH
- J. Smith LF
- A. Giménez SS
- B. Valenzuela C
- E. Clement 2B
Toronto will start Spencer Miles as the opener, as it's a bullpen game with Spencer Arrighetti getting the bulk of the innings.
Kirk getting the day off isn't a surprise, as Valenzuela has been catching and starting a lot on Sunday to give Kirk the day off in the series finale.
Valenzuela is a great defensive catcher with a cannon of an arm, yet his bat has struggled as of late. He's hitting .217 with 8 home runs and 21 RBIs. However, in his last 7 games, he's hitting .105 with 0 home runs and 0 RBIs, while striking out 5 times.
Toronto Right Now
The Blue Jays have struggled all year, and now their playoff fate is likely sealed.
Toronto lost the first two games of a three-game road series against Texas, which seemingly ended their playoff hopes. The Blue Jays have been blown out in both of their games against the Rangers, which is frustrating for the team.
Jose Soriano struggled in the outing, which was frustrating for the team as the Blue Jays sent Dylan Cease and Soriano, their two best pitchers, in the first two games.
"We're still positive. Doesn't matter the result, we're still positive," said Soriano. "We're not going to win every game we play. The other team's trying to win, too. So, we try to control what we can control and play one game at a time."
The Blue Jays will go on a three-game road trip against the Baltimore Orioles starting on Monday. Toronto will end its season with a three-game home series against the Cincinnati Reds.
Toronto likely has to finish the year 7-0 to have any shot of making the playoffs.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Toronto Blue Jays Announce Brandon Valenzuela News During Rangers Series appeared first on HEAVY.

item.title: [en.as.com] Dylan Cease said he would “die on the battlefield” for Blue Jays before disastrous start
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Bubel
item.description: Dylan Cease made an emphatic promise to the Toronto Blue Jays before their crucial series against the Texas Rangers, saying he was ready to “die on the battlefield” for his team. The Blue Jays needed Cease to deliver in the opener of a three-game series in Arlington on Friday, with Toronto’s playoff hopes hanging by a thread. Instead, the right-hander endured one of his roughest outings of the season as the Rangers cruised to a 7-1 victory. Dylan Cease pitched 2.2 innings in Texas tonight, his s
item.content:encoded:
Dylan Cease made an emphatic promise to the Toronto Blue Jays before their crucial series against the Texas Rangers, saying he was ready to “die on the battlefield” for his team.
The Blue Jays needed Cease to deliver in the opener of a three-game series in Arlington on Friday, with Toronto’s playoff hopes hanging by a thread. Instead, the right-hander endured one of his roughest outings of the season as the Rangers cruised to a 7-1 victory.
Dylan Cease pitched 2.2 innings in Texas tonight, his shortest outing of the season
He allowed one earned run on three hits and a season-high six walks, but a Blue Jays error resulted in three unearned runs pic.twitter.com/34yYIK4i48
Cease had described the start as the biggest he had made since joining Toronto, although he insisted that he approached it no differently from any other.
“It is, yeah, but right now every single start is just as important as the next,” Cease said before the game. “I treat every single start the same. They all matter the same. Obviously, the stakes are what they are now because we’ve dug ourselves into a little hole, but I don’t treat any start differently.”
The interview was conducted ahead of Friday’s game by Alex Withers on behalf of Casino.org Canada, with the comments made available to AS for use.
Dylan Cease accepted responsibility for Blue Jays’ playoff push
Toronto’s pitching staff has been hit by injuries, increasing the importance of every available starter down the stretch. Cease said he understood the responsibility but didn’t want to allow the playoff pressure to affect his mindset.
“I definitely feel the responsibility, but I wouldn’t say I feel any pressure,” Cease said. “I just want to get the job done and I’m always going to put the effort into it to achieve this. I’m going to die on the battlefield for my team.”
Cease also explained how he tries to turn the pressure of a playoff race into something productive rather than allowing it to become a distraction.
“I care deeply about winning and I want nothing more than to win, but I don’t let it get to a point mentally to where it debilitates me,” he said. “I let it get me to the point where it gives me motivation and focus.”
That mindset was put to the test almost immediately. Cease allowed four runs, three hits, and six walks in just 2⅔ innings against Texas. Only one of the four runs was earned, but the six walks were a season high and Toronto never recovered from an early deficit.
Dylan Cease tonight:
2.2 IP | 3 H | 4 R (1 ER) | 6 BB | 3 K
It's his shortest outing of the season. pic.twitter.com/j3DOvrPbDG
Cease struggled as Blue Jays’ playoff hopes took another hit
The result was damaging because Toronto entered the series already two games behind the Chicago White Sox for the American League’s final wild-card position. The Blue Jays are now 76-78, while the Rangers improved to 77-77 with the victory. Toronto has eight games remaining in the regular season.
Rangers take the lead on sloppy defense by the Blue Jays! Texas and Toronto are both two games back of the final Wild Card spot pic.twitter.com/WGHhPod75Z
— Talkin' Baseball (@TalkinBaseball_) September 19, 2026
Cease had entered Friday’s game with an 11-5 record and a 2.38 ERA according to the statistics available before his start. His season ERA now stands at 2.40 despite the difficult outing.
Before the game, Cease acknowledged the urgency facing Toronto and said the Blue Jays had to maintain their belief that they could still reach the postseason.
“You have to have that mindset. You have to have that belief. It doesn’t pay to be pessimistic,” Cease said. “We’re going out every day and we’re fighting hard.”
He also admitted that Toronto had not been as consistent as they needed to be throughout the season, while arguing that the team had played better baseball during the second half.
“I believe we’ve had a really solid second half,” Cease said. “We’ve genuinely played good baseball, so I think we’re staying level-headed and we know what we’ve got to do.”
Dylan Cease called every game a “must-win”
The Blue Jays still have two games remaining against Texas, but Friday’s loss made their margin for error even smaller.
“Of course, if we win the series it’s going to put us in a way better position than not,” Cease said before the opener. “I truly mean I’m going to treat every single game the same the rest of the way. Every single game that you ever play is a must-win for us.”
Toronto will try to respond Saturday when José Soriano takes the mound against Texas right-hander Cal Quantrill. Soriano entered the game with a 12-7 record and a 3.56 ERA.
Cease’s message before the series was clear. Toronto needed to embrace the pressure, stay focused and fight until the final out.
“I think at this point it’s just laying it all out there and seeing how the chips lie,” he said.
On Friday, though, Toronto’s most important starter lasted just eight outs and the Rangers moved another step closer to the Blue Jays in the playoff race.

item.title: [Toronto Star] Blue Jays vs. Rangers: Dylan Cease and Toronto’s fading wild-card hopes hit the wall in Texas
item.dc:creator: Gregor Chisholm
item.description: Dylan Cease appears to have run out of gas, and the same could be said about the Blue Jays’ ability to make the playoffs. Cease has been carrying the starting rotation and middling offence for most of the year. The heavy lifting clearly took a toll for the stretch run. The 30-year-old right-hander allowed four runs and couldn’t get out of t
item.content:encoded:
Dylan Cease appears to have run out of gas, and the same could be said about the Blue Jays’ ability to make the playoffs.
Cease has been carrying the starting rotation and middling offence for most of the year. The heavy lifting clearly took a toll for the stretch run.
The velocity on Cease’s fastball has been steadily declining for several weeks and dipped even lower in a 7-1 road loss to the Texas Rangers on Friday night. The 30-year-old right-hander allowed four runs and couldn’t get out of the third inning of the pivotal series opener.
Meanwhile, the Cleveland Guardians won to move into first place in the American League Central, while the Chicago White Sox lost. That means the Jays trail the White Sox by two games for the final wild-card spot, and they do not own the tiebreaker.
Cease’s poor showing should also eliminate him from Cy Young consideration. That honour will likely go to Yankees right-hander Cam Schlittler, who has pitched more innings (184 2/3 vs. 169) with a lower ERA (1.95 vs. 2.40) and fewer walks/hits per inning pitched (0.90 vs. 1.10).
It wasn’t supposed to end this way. Through the first five months, Cease was consistently hitting the upper-90s in miles per hour with his fastball. That high velocity combined with a wipeout slider turned him into the major-league leader in strikeouts and a front-runner to win the first Cy Young of his career.
The warning signs started earlier this month. Against the Athletics on Sept. 7, his average fastball velocity fell below 95 m.p.h. for the first time since 2023. The problems continued in Cease’s next outing versus the Baltimore Orioles, when he failed to average 95 m.p.h. or higher in back-to-back starts for the first time in the big leagues.
The lack of heat became an even bigger issue in Texas. Through the first couple of innings, his fastball sat in the 91-to-93-m.p.h. range. By the time he walked off the field with his team trailing by four, his average was still only 93.6 m.p.h., a career low.
The other issue against Texas was that his command was all over the place. Cease threw just 36 of 74 pitches for strikes with an alarming six walks, his most since Aug. 16 of last year.
Every inning, every pitch was a grind. Cease walked two in the first inning, but escaped unscathed. There were two more walks and a single by Nicky López in the second to load the bases.
The turning point came on the next ground ball when shortstop Ernie Clement made an ill-advised throw to third base. He was trying to get the force out, but his throw bounced off Jake Burger’s helmet and ricocheted down the line as two runners scored.
Cease then served up a sacrifice fly to Ezequiel Durán before Corey Seager added an RBI double and the Rangers jumped in front 4-0. Cease returned for the third, but loaded the bases again before he was replaced by Brendan Cellucci.
The late-season swoon will likely teach the Jays some valuable lessons about how to handle Cease in the future. On the surface, 169 innings is a reasonable workload. But this isn’t about how many outs he recorded, it’s about how many pitches he threw while doing it.
There were four consecutive starts in April and May when Cease threw at least 106 pitches, followed by seven straight starts of at least 102 in June and July, including a season-high 120. There was another stretch of four starts with 100-plus pitches in August.
The Jays continue to insist Cease is fine and there are no injury concerns. That’s probably true — if not, it would be a fireable offence — but it doesn’t change the fact that he has clearly worn down and no longer resembles the pitcher he was through the first five months.
The bigger issue is that the loss was a major blow to the lethargic Jays’ playoff hopes. They have eight games left to make up three games in the standings; Toronto owns the tiebreaker with the Guardians, but not with the White Sox.
After playing mediocre baseball through the first four months, the Jays had little margin for error in August and September. They needed to be at their best over the last couple of weeks and instead were at their worst.
The season isn’t technically over, but a 4-7 stretch has put them on the brink. Their only shot now is winning almost all of their remaining games while hoping for a total collapse by the White Sox.

item.title: [The Killeen Daily Herald] Corey Seager's RBI double helps Rangers beat sloppy Blue Jays 7-1 and close gap in playoff race
item.dc:creator: SCHUYLER DIXON
item.description: ARLINGTON, Texas (AP) — Corey Seager had an RBI double in a four-run second inning fueled by a throwing error, and the Texas Rangers beat the Toronto Blue Jays 7-1 on Friday night in the opener of a series matching AL playoff chasers. The Rangers (77-77) reached .500 for a majors-leading 23rd time and pulled within one game of the White Sox for the third and final AL wild-card spot, although Chicago has the tiebreaker. The defending AL champion Blue Jays (76-78) are two games back in the wild-ca
item.content:encoded:
ARLINGTON, Texas (AP) — Corey Seager had an RBI double in a four-run second inning fueled by a throwing error, and the Texas Rangers beat the Toronto Blue Jays 7-1 on Friday night in the opener of a series matching AL playoff chasers.
The Rangers (77-77) reached .500 for a majors-leading 23rd time and pulled within one game of the White Sox for the third and final AL wild-card spot, although Chicago has the tiebreaker. The defending AL champion Blue Jays (76-78) are two games back in the wild-card race.
Texas also closed the gap on Houston by pulling even with the Astros atop the AL West, but the Rangers would have to win the division outright to finish ahead of their in-state rival. Houston lost to Atlanta 6-2.
The Rangers took the lead in the second on Evan Carter's bases-loaded grounder that scored Wyatt Langford, and Jake Burger also came home when shortstop Ernie Clement's throw trying to force him out at third bounced wide of the bag into foul territory. Seager made it 4-0 with his double.
Dylan Cease (11-6) walked a season-high six among his first 15 batters and was replaced with two outs in the third after throwing 38 balls and 36 strikes.
Six of the Texas runs were unearned as the Blue Jays walked 10 and had three throwing errors, two by third baseman Kazuma Okamoto.
Trevor Williams (2-0) finished with four scoreless innings after starter Kumar Rocker took a 4-0 lead into the fifth but couldn't finish and was replaced by Tyler Alexander.
Toronto's Nathan Lukes had the longest active hitting streak in the majors stopped at 13 games when he was replaced by pinch-hitter Davis Schneider in the fifth. Lukes was 0 for 2 with a deep liner that Carter, the center fielder, ran down at the wall in right center.
Up next
Blue Jays RHP José Soriano (12-7, 3.56 ERA) is set to face Texas RHP Cal Quantrill (9-5, 2.90) on Saturday.

item.content:encoded:
The Toronto Blue Jays made franchise history when they gave Dylan Cease a record-setting seven-year contract in free agency for $210 million.
They surely would’ve hoped he could make history on the mound for them, too.
On Friday night, that’s what Cease did.
It just wasn’t the kind of history that the Blue Jays would’ve hoped for from Cease.
Dylan Cease Unfortunate History
Cease threw a pitching line that had never happened before in MLB history.
Against the Rangers, he went 2.2 innings, allowing three hits and walking six while giving up one earned run and striking out three.
That combination of five statistics had never happened:
🚨 PITCHERGAMI 🚨
Dylan Cease just threw a line that has NEVER happened in MLB history:
2.2 IP | 3 H | 1 ER | 6 BB | 3 K
TOR @ TEX
That’s the 389th Pitchergami of 2026 and 1 of 83,614+ unique lines on record.
— Pitchergami (@pitchergami) September 19, 2026
At first glance, it’s amazing that there are still pitching lines that have never happened before.
Then you look at this one, and it kind of makes sense.
Just in the walks and hits, Cease gave up nine baserunners while only getting eight outs. Generally, that would give up more than one earned run.
And in a past era, a pitcher that had given up only one earned run may be left in the game even with all the walks.
But everything factored together gave Cease this specific line, and it’s certainly a unique one.
Dylan Cease Trended This Way
The thing is, there was already a potential cause for concern entering the night.
A post on social media earlier in the day showed how Cease’s velocity had declined all season long.
In April, he averaged 97.8 miles per hour on his four-seam fastball
Cease kept that exact mark on his heater in May, 97.8 MPH again.
It declined to 97.4 miles per hour in June, a small enough decrease to not worry much.
Then in July, Cease was down to 96.7 MPH on his four-seam fastball on average. His August velocity was an average of 95.8 miles per hour.
And in September, Cease entered Friday night’s start at 95.3 miles per hour on average on his four-seam fastball.
It doesn’t automatically mean he’s hurt, but it also doesn’t seem like it can be ideal.
And on Friday night, Cease’s results finally reflected the potential that he’s got something a little off with him.
Fastball velocity doesn’t inherently impact walk numbers, so if you were trying to create a correlation here, it’d be more that Cease’s arm isn’t at full strength, which impacted both velocity and control.
Of course, there are other possible explanations.
All that’s clear is that Cease didn’t have it on Friday night, and it cost him.

item.content:encoded:
Things didn't go as planned for the Toronto Blue Jays and ace Dylan Cease to open their pivotal series against the Texas Rangers.
Cease battled both his command and velocity throughout his start against the Rangers and wasn't able to complete the third inning before turning the ball over to manager John Schneider.
The 30-year-old walked off the mound after 2.2 innings of work, having allowed three hits, four runs (one earned), and six walks while striking out three.
It marked his shortest appearance of the season.
Cease worked around some trouble early, inducing an inning-ending double play off the bat of Brandon Nimmo in the first after issuing a pair of one-out walks.
But the free passes and an untimely error cost the righty in the second.
After loading the bases with one out in the frame, Rangers centre-fielder Evan Carter chopped a ground ball up the middle that took a weird bounce off the mound and went straight to Blue Jays shortstop Ernie Clement.
Clement opted to try for an out at third, but his throw hit Jake Burger in the back and caromed down the left-field line, allowing two runs to score on the play.
Texas then added two extra runs on a sacrifice fly from Ezequiel Duran and an RBI double by Corey Seager.
Cease came back out for the third but saw his pitch count climb as he loaded the bases once again on a pair of walks and a Nicky Lopez single. He did bounce back to get the second out of the inning by striking out Elias Díaz before Brendan Cellucci entered and escaped the jam unscathed with a punchout of his own.
When all was said and done for Cease, he had tossed 74 pitches and 36 strikes while averaging 93.6 m.p.h. with his fastball — 3.3 m.p.h. slower than his season average of 96.9. — continuing a troubling trend of diminished velocity for the all-star.
Toronto had bumped Cease's scheduled start up a day so that he was opening this series in Arlington on regular rest, rather than leveraging Thursday's off-day to give the eight-year veteran an extra day and have him pitch on turn in Saturday's contest.

item.content:encoded:
The Toronto Blue Jays pulled off a blockbuster move at the trade deadline to acquire Jose Soriano.
Toronto is beginning a three-game road series against the Texas Rangers on the road on Friday. The Blue Jays have 9 games left and are 2 games back of a Wild Card spot.
The Blue Jays will start Dylan Cease on Friday, with Jose Soriano getting the ball on Saturday.
Dylan Cease Comments on Jose Soriano
Before the Blue Jays began their three-game series against the Rangers, Cease was asked about Soriano.
Soriano and Cease have formed a two-headed monster atop the Blue Jays rotation. With the Blue Jays, Soriano has had success, and Cease admits he’s impressed with him and his stuff.
“Soriano will step up. He’s nasty. He sits upper 90s with a bowling ball sinker and nasty off-speed, so every time he takes the ball, I feel really good about it,” Cease said, via Casino.org. “Anyone that takes the ball now will be a difference maker and has a chance to be a difference maker. Everyone in the team knows where we’re at. Everyone knows that every pitch is important, that every game is important, so we’ll see who steps up and how it all plays out.”
With the Blue Jays, Soriano is 3-1 with a 4.27 ERA in 8 starts. Although the numbers aren’t as dominant as Toronto may want, he is still an impact pitcher for the team.
Toronto Blue Jays Right Now
The Blue Jays enter their road series against the Rangers 2 games back of the Cleveland Guardians for the final Wild Card spot.
Toronto is also tied with the Rangers, so this series is pivotal and Cease said the Blue Jays remain confident in their group.
“I think we feel great,” Cease said. “We don’t ever go into any game or any series not expecting to do well. We have been playing well in the second half of the season and I believe we’ve had a lot of improvement in our play. We’ve genuinely played good baseball, so I think we’re staying level-headed and we know what we’ve got to do. We can still make the playoffs. I think that you have to have that mindset. You have to have that belief. It doesn’t pay to be pessimistic.
“We’re going out every day and we’re fighting hard, and to be honest with you, we feel like we’ve fought hard all year. It obviously hasn’t been our year in a lot of ways, and we haven’t done what we needed to do and want to do for a lot of the season, but the fact that we’re still in it and we’re still close really says it all. We’re all just taking it day by day and continuing to not give up that fight. Of course, if we win the series it’s going to put us in a way better position than not. I truly mean I’m going to treat every single game the same the rest of the way. Every single game that you ever play is a must-win for us.”
The Blue Jays are 76-77.
